expected_findings.description: Returning a generator makes the function's result single-use, but `summarise` (lines 24-28, unchanged) iterates its argument twice: once in `sum(1 for _ in records)` and again in the `[r.key for r in records]` comprehension. The first pass exhausts the generator, so the second yields nothing. That was correct while `parse_records` returned a list. Every caller passing the new return value straight to `summarise` now gets a correct count with an empty `keys` list - a silently wrong result rather than an error.

notes:
PILOT CASE - Python. Not part of the frozen Rust benchmark and not included in any headline figure.

Single-consumption of an iterator has no Rust analogue that behaves this way silently: Rust's borrow checker and `Iterator` semantics would force the issue at compile time, and a consumed iterator cannot be silently re-read into an empty result. This case exists to test a defect class the Rust benchmark structurally cannot contain.

The defect is also split across two functions in the SAME file, which makes it a different investigation shape from p01 and p03 - the reviewer does not need to leave the changed file, but does need to connect the change at line 11 to the unchanged consumer at line 24. A reviewer reading only the diff hunk sees a defensible laziness optimisation.

Why the tests miss it: all three call `list(parse_records(...))` before doing anything, materialising the generator first. `test_summarise_counts_a_list` passes an explicit `list(...)`, so it exercises `summarise` only against the old contract and passes unchanged.

Verified by execution: `summarise(parse_records(LINES))` returns count 3 with keys [], where the pre-change version returned count 3 with keys ['a','b','c'].

also_accept covers StateManagement and ApiContract.

ANCHORING CORRECTION, recorded because it was found via a result rather than by review. This finding was originally anchored at `summarise` (lines 24-28), the consumer. That is a defensible place to fix the defect, but it is the only ground-truth finding in the whole project - 1 of 12 - anchored OUTSIDE the changed hunk; every other case anchors at the changed code. The anchor was moved to the changed lines for consistency with that convention, which is objectively checkable and now enforced by `vcr check`.

The correction was prompted by the advanced arm reporting this defect at lines 15-19 with a fully correct diagnosis naming `summarise`, the double iteration, and the empty result - and being scored a false positive plus a false negative for it. Both the as-authored and corrected pilot figures are reported in docs/pilot-python.md so the effect of the change is visible rather than absorbed.
